image_description: A person wearing a white t-shirt and blue jeans is holding a large, reddish-brown wooden wind instrument diagonally across their body. The instrument has a U-shaped structure with a flared bell at the top and a curved metal neck (bocal) extending from it. The wood appears polished, and there are visible metal keys and mechanisms along the body of the instrument.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long wooden wind instrument of considerable height when assembled.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument spans nearly the full height of the seated/torso-visible subject, indicating significant length consistent with a bassoon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive U-shape when viewed from front with bell pointing upward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument clearly exhibits the characteristic U-shape (boot joint at bottom, long joints rising up) with the bell flare oriented upwards.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Conical bore that doubles back on itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The internal bore structure is not visible from the exterior; this feature cannot be visually verified without X-ray or cross-section views.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Curved metal bocal mouthpiece tube at top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A curved metal tube (bocal) is clearly visible emerging from the top joint near the subject's face/mouth area.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Numerous metal keys and tone holes distributed along length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Multiple silver-colored metal keys, rods, and key guards are visible along the wooden body of the instrument.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bell flares outward at top and instrument held diagonally across body when played.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bell section is visibly flared and positioned at the top right of the frame. The instrument is held diagonally across the player's torso, consistent with playing posture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dark reddish-brown polished wood finish maple or rosewood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wood has a distinct deep reddish-brown hue with specular highlights indicating a polished varnish finish, typical of maple bassoons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal keys are silver or gold-plated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible keys and mechanical linkages appear silver-colored (nickel-silver or silver-plated), contrasting with the dark wood.
The main body segments are clearly constructed from turned wood, joined by metal ferrules.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The skin texture on the neck and lower face appears slightly smudged or painterly compared to the sharper fabric textures, suggesting minor generative smoothing or compression artifacts.

The fingers of the left hand (lower on the instrument) appear somewhat fused or indistinct where they contact the keys. The anatomical definition of individual digits is weak, and the grip looks physically ambiguous.
The vertical line of the wall corner on the right side shows slight waviness or bending, inconsistent with rigid architectural geometry.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification of the instrument as a bassoon and distinguish it from similar woodwinds like the contrabassoon or oboe.
To audit the structural integrity of the human hands and arms interacting with the instrument, specifically checking for finger fusion or impossible joint angles.
To verify that the complex mechanical keywork is topologically connected correctly to the wooden body and does not have floating or merged components.
To assess the overall coherence of lighting, shadows, and texture consistency between the organic subject and the inorganic instrument.

focus_areas: Wood grain continuity and polish reflections
